item.title: Re: Anomalous defense
item.content:encoded:
You can write about anything you want! It will only stay on the site if people like it enough to rate it positively though.

In-universe, SCPs generally aren't used for defense unless absolutely necessary, because their whole nature is that they're unpredictable (and often unique, which isn't good when you need to equip an entire army). 914 in particular tends to be pretty defiant and unhelpful with what it makes, so it probably wouldn't be a good idea to rely on it for your defense.

That said, I can see a pretty entertaining tale coming out of this if 914 refuses to make them any kind of normal weapon and only makes weird ones, and the Foundation just rolls with it and finds interesting ways to use them. Making the weapons interesting rather than just powerful would be the key to it in any case.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm struggling to understand how you can really write anything approaching hard sci-fi in a scenario like this. The "battle" would be so lopsided as to end the story before it even began, like a fight scene between a nuclear missile and a little fluffy bunny.

To attack us, aliens would have to get here, necessitating something like FTL travel. In the extremely unlikely event that the only technological advantage they have over us is making physical objects move that fast, they could just throw a rock at us and watch as Earth got turned into chunks. Or for even more fun, use something like a Shkadov thruster to throw a sun at us. Humans already have technology capable of destroying all sapient life on the planet, just detonate some big nukes and then everybody dies. Given a thousand-year technological head start (let alone a million year head start), they'd have weapons that not only could we not make, but would not have the slightest clue how they work.

Although… there is a way I can think of to create a scenario with technology that was at least kind of comparable in power - actual magic. A wizard did it. For example, let's use teleportation, which shows up all over this wiki already. Imagine that the Foundation accidentally opens a permanent portal to a hostile world, except unlike the other skip entries, they opened up a portal to the homeworld of a non-anomalous world. The Foundation is always bumbling their way into really weird places, it actually seems more likely that they would end up in a different spot in the real universe instead of the usual eldritch horror dimension full of skyscraper-sized monsters made of insanity lightning.

If we're using magic to hand-wave issues like FTL travel, though, you'd almost certainly have to use skips to explain how two civilizations are at the same technological level at exactly the same time despite living in a 13 billion year old universe. I can't think of how we could keep this premise from drifting back into science-fantasy instead of science fiction.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
[With sincerity rather than sarcasm] Sounds like the basis of a dissenting article right there. If you did a good job with writing it up, I'd probably even upvote it myself.

I'll reiterate my out-of-universe reasoning for the assumption, though:

Basically, this means we're aiming for "hard" science fiction. Why? (Especially when so much of this wiki is "soft" science fiction?)

  • There are a surprising dearth of alien invasion stories which have any sort of grounding in real-world science.
  • The goal here is not to worldbuild anomalous science fiction aliens and technology or claim alien origin of existing SCPs. Do NOT use SCPs as the hypothetical aliens or alien tech. No, not even especially not 682.
  • Who knows what sort of aliens might exist, and how they might better understand the universe and its natural laws than humanity? But don't sell humans too short. The Foundation is one of the world's foremost scientific entities and has access to entities which defy conventional understanding of scientific laws. And yet the Foundation still operates under the basic assumption that the scientific laws known by the non-affiliated scientific community are correct (or at minimum less wrong than any other known alternative) except in a tiny handful of cases. The point is, SCPs are anomalies which may be impossible to replicate, no matter what galaxy you're from.
  • There's plenty of reason to be downright terrified of scientifically plausible extraterrestrial threats; from a pragmatic standpoint, it makes more sense to develop plans for fighting the devil that you know first.
  • Perhaps most significantly, assuming hard science for aliens and their technology keeps all collaborators on the same page.

Also, there's no indication that Heimdall is the only contingency planning the Foundation is doing related to extraterrestrials. They might probably would have other contingency plans for the various "what-ifs" of soft-scifi alien invasions. Beyond the aforementioned reasons, I'm trying to avoid incurring the wrath of Senior Staff by opening the floodgates to bad articles on lolphysics that are only tangentially related to what this site is actually about.

item.content:encoded:
Hostile Extraterrestrials (HEs) will possess no technology forbidden by the laws of physics.

Since both Dr Wondertainment and The Factory can mass-produce anomalies, I don't think this would be a reasonable assumption. I think better rationals for this point would be: 1) you can't do any planning if you throw into the scenario "the HEs might have lots and lots of unknown anomalies, which being unknown could be capable of anything", and 2) if the HEs have mass-produced anomalous technology and weapons then Earth/humanity is unavoidably screwed, so we should focus our planning on scenarios where there's actually a chance of avoiding becoming screwed.
